To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social entrepreneurs employ 39 strategies that vary across fields of practices and time; that these strategies can be classified into six meta-strategies (social innovation, community development, advocacy, capacity building, system reform, and social entrepreneurship); and that four new strategies (system reform, physical capital, evidence-based practices and prototyping) are identified.

social entrepreneurs employ 39 strategies that vary in terms of resources, specificity and mode of participation; they employ six meta-strategies that vary in terms in terms of the type of resources they use, and the type of change they make; they employ four meta-strategies that have not been previously identified in the SE literature.
social entrepreneurs use a total of 2,334 strategies that vary across fields of practices, time, resources, specificity, and modes of participation.

the strategies employed by SEs are not only diverse and dynamic, but also context-specific, and they vary across fields of practices and time.
